name: alceml-pages
command: (not reproducible locally: the pages are written by a storage node, not by a formatting tool)
note: worker-4 /dev/sdc of the OKD lab cluster: a device a previous simplyblock deployment took, still carrying that deployment's data, whose ALCEML_STORAGE superblock at offset 0 is gone. The first 1060864 bytes are zero; at 1060864 there is an ALCEML_PAGEv2 page header, and its mapping blocks run to 1077376. That grid repeats every 2105344 bytes to about 1.2 TB, after which the device turns into a region of 64-byte records the catalog does not know. The tail is 1911087 non-zero bytes of it. Captured at a region of 2 MiB rather than the default 1 MiB because the first page header is 12288 bytes past where a 1 MiB head stops. At that default the device reads Blank, which is the wanted answer under the head-only zero rule and the reason this capture is kept: it holds the bytes a format would destroy. Before that rule it read Foreign, and the deployment of 2026-09-28 was declined on every such disk.
